hero.title: The Triratna of Buddhism
hero.description: The Three Jewels represent the foundational triad of refuge in Buddhism, essential for attaining enlightenment and ending the cycle of rebirth.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Historical evolution of the Triratna from the life of Buddha to the institutionalized Sangha.

cards.details: Life of Siddhartha Gautama; conceptualization of the Buddha and Dhamma during his ministry.
First Buddhist Council at Rajgriha; the Sangha begins formalizing the Vinaya Pitaka to regulate the community.
Ashoka's patronage formalizes the three refuges as the core identity of Buddhist followers across the Mauryan Empire.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Prelims
mnemonics.description: Remember the sequence using the 'B.D.S' framework.

items.title: B.D.S
items.decryption: B (Buddha/The Teacher), D (Dhamma/The Teaching), S (Sangha/The Community). Think of it as: Source -> Content -> Vehicle.

items: Jainism also has a 'Triratna' (Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct). Do not confuse these with the Buddhist Triratna.
The Sangha in early Buddhism refers specifically to the monastic community, not all lay followers.

deepDive.description: Master the key concepts and dimensions of this topic.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Tenets

  • Buddha: The enlightened one, the guide.
  • Dhamma: The cosmic law and Buddha's doctrine.
  • Sangha: The assembly of monks/nuns.

Significance

  • Spiritual Refuge (Sarana).
  • Basis of initiation.
  • Core of the 'Refuge Formula'.

Mindmap Overview

  • 1. Buddha (The Guide)
    • Historical figure (Gautama).
    • Potential for Buddhahood in all beings.
    • Symbol of enlightenment (Bodhi).
  • 2. Dhamma (The Path)
    • Four Noble Truths.
    • Eightfold Path (Astangika Marga).
    • Universal law (Dharma).
  • 3. Sangha (The Community)
    • Monastic order (Bhikshus & Bhikshunis).
    • Preservation of oral traditions.
    • Social cohesion and moral guidance.
